passages.title: The Loom of the Night
passages.content:
She sits upon the mountain's crest,
A silent watcher in the west.
Her hands, a blur of silver light,
Begin to weave the looming night.

A blanket of obsidian spun,
To cool the embers of the sun.
With gossamer of comet tails,
She patches up the astral sails.

And when the mortals weep or mourn,
She takes the threads that they have torn,
And knits them into shooting stars,
To hide the universe's scars.

passages.title: Mangrove Restoration in Visayas
passages.content:
Coastal erosion and severe typhoons have long plagued the Visayas region. In response, a massive mangrove restoration project was launched in 2021. Mangroves act as natural buffers against storm surges, their complex root systems dissipating wave energy. Beyond protection, they serve as critical nurseries for marine life, boosting local fishery yields.

However, initial efforts saw mixed results due to improper species selection. The table below details the survival rates of three species planted in the Panay area after two years.

| Species | Planted | Survived | Growth Rate (cm/year) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rhizophora | 5,000 | 4,200 | 15 |
| Avicennia | 3,000 | 1,800 | 25 |
| Sonneratia | 2,000 | 1,500 | 20 |

The project learned that planting Avicennia in the seaward zones, despite its lower survival rate here, is essential due to its high resistance to salinity and inundation. Community involvement has been the true linchpin. Local fisherfolk, who initially viewed the mangroves as obstacles to boat navigation, are now the primary caretakers, realizing that the temporary inconvenience is far outweighed by long-term ecological and economic benefits.

passages.title: The Digital Divide: Two Perspectives on AI in Education
passages.content:
Passage 3A: Speech by a Technology Advocate
The integration of artificial intelligence in Philippine classrooms is not merely a luxury; it is an imperative. As the global economy shifts toward automation, our students must be digitally fluent. AI-driven adaptive learning software allows for personalized education, tailoring lessons to a student's pace and identifying knowledge gaps in real time. This level of efficiency cannot be achieved by a single teacher managing a class of fifty. Opponents argue that technology diminishes the human element, but we must ask: isn't preparing our youth for the realities of the 21st century the most profoundly human service we can offer?

Passage 3B: Essay by a Veteran Educator
We are rushing headlong into a digitized classroom, blinded by the shiny promise of efficiency. While AI can certainly deliver facts and grade multiple-choice tests, education is not simply data transfer. It is character formation. A machine cannot detect the nuance of a student's sudden silence, nor can it inspire a child through genuine empathy. Furthermore, framing AI as an educational panacea ignores the glaring infrastructural deficits in our rural schools. We are at risk of widening the digital divide, creating a two-tiered system where the privileged converse with algorithms, while the marginalized remain disconnected.

passages.title: The Approaching Storm
passages.content:
The radio crackled with static, a telltale sign that Signal No. 3 was imminent. Lolo Tasyo did not flinch; his eyes, calloused not just by age but by countless tempests, simply surveyed the tin roof of their modest home. "Hurry, Nene," he instructed his granddaughter, handing her a bundle of thick nylon ropes. "The wind is like a hungry dog. If you give it an edge to bite, it will tear the whole roof off."

Nene nodded, her hands trembling as she tied the ropes to the sturdy concrete pillars, anchoring the corrugated sheets. She had always dreaded the monsoons, but watching her grandfather move with methodical calm offered a strange comfort. He wasn't fighting the storm; he was preparing to endure it. "We don't conquer the rain, Nene," Lolo Tasyo murmured, pulling a knot tight. "We just make sure our foundation is stronger than its anger."

passages.title: How to Weave a Traditional Banig
passages.content:
The traditional Filipino banig (sleeping mat) is a testament to patience and artistry. While materials vary by region, the fundamental procedure remains consistent.

Step 1: Harvesting. Mature leaves are carefully cut to avoid damaging the main plant.
Step 2: Stripping and Sun-drying. The thorny edges are removed, and the leaves are stripped into uniform widths. They are laid out in the sun for two to three days until they turn a light brown hue.
Step 3: Dyeing. The dried strips are boiled in pots with vibrant chemical or natural dyes to create colors like magenta, green, and yellow.
Step 4: Flattening. Once dyed and dried again, the strips are flattened using a piece of smooth hardwood.
Step 5: Weaving. The artisan weaves the strips using intricate geometric patterns.

| Mat Size | Prep Time | Weaving Time | Total Time |
|---|---|---|---|
| Single | 3 days | 2 days | 5 days |
| Double | 3 days | 4 days | 7 days |
| Family | 4 days | 6 days | 10 days |

The meticulous process ensures that the banig is not only functional but also a durable family heirloom, mitigating the effects of hot tropical nights through its breathable weave. This craft is entirely reliant on human hands; no machine can replicate the tight, custom tension of an expert weaver.

passages.title: The Cost of Moving Forward
passages.content:
The push for the Public Utility Vehicle (PUV) Modernization Program has sparked fiery debates across the archipelago. The central argument of the state is environmental and safety-driven: replacing the ubiquitous, smoke-belching traditional jeepneys with Euro-4 compliant or electric vehicles. This is an undeniable ecological necessity.

However, the transition demands a critical look at economic equity. A modern jeepney costs upwards of 2,500,000 pesos. Even with a government equity subsidy of 160,000 pesos, the financial burden placed on a single operator is staggering.

[Editorial Cartoon Description: A small, exhausted jeepney driver in tattered clothes is depicted carrying a massive, incredibly heavy modern minibus on his back, his knees buckling. A giant government official in a sharp suit stands comfortably nearby, smiling brightly and dropping a single tiny coin labeled 'Subsidy' into a tin cup held by the driver.]

If we mandate modernization without providing a commercially viable transition plan, we are essentially punishing the poor for a systemic failure. Progress cannot be genuinely called progress if it leaves the most vulnerable sectors in the dust. We must rethink the financial structuring of this program before the backbone of our public transport snaps.

questions.questionText: A local cooperative receives an order for 2 Single mats and 1 Family mat. Assuming they have 3 weavers and each weaver works on exactly one mat from start to finish (prep and weaving), how many total days of labor (the sum of all individual days worked by the 3 weavers) will it take to fulfill this order based on the table?

choices.A: 15 days
choices.B: 20 days
choices.C: 22 days
choices.D: 24 days

questions.rationale: From the table, a Single mat takes 5 total days. A Family mat takes 10 total days. Two Single mats = 5 + 5 = 10 days. One Family mat = 10 days. Total days of labor = 10 + 10 = 20 days.
objectives: interpret a short embedded informational element such as a table, graph, or similar text-based data

questions.questionText: In the final paragraph, what does 'mitigating' mean?

choices.A: Worsening or aggravating
choices.B: Enhancing or increasing
choices.C: Lessening the severity of
choices.D: Completely preventing

questions.rationale: The text says the mat is 'mitigating the effects of hot tropical nights through its breathable weave', meaning it lessens the discomfort of the heat.
objectives: determine the meaning of words and phrases in context

questions.questionText: According to the table, how much longer does it take to weave a Family mat compared to prepping it?

choices.A: 1 day
choices.B: 2 days
choices.C: 3 days
choices.D: 4 days

questions.rationale: The table shows that for a Family mat, Prep Time is 4 days and Weaving Time is 6 days. 6 - 4 = 2 days.
objectives: interpret a short embedded informational element such as a table, graph, or similar text-based data

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements from the passage is an opinion?

choices.A: The traditional Filipino banig is a testament to patience and artistry.
choices.B: Mature leaves are carefully cut to avoid damaging the main plant.
choices.C: The dried strips are boiled in pots with chemical or natural dyes.
choices.D: A Single mat requires 3 days of prep time.

questions.rationale: Calling the banig a 'testament to patience and artistry' is a subjective qualitative evaluation, whereas the other choices describe factual procedures or data.
objectives: distinguish fact from opinion

questions.questionText: What conclusion can be drawn about the relationship between the size of the mat and its production process?

choices.A: Prep time increases significantly more than weaving time as the mat gets larger.
choices.B: The larger the mat, the greater the proportion of total time spent on weaving compared to prep time.
choices.C: Mat size has no effect on prep time.
choices.D: A Double mat requires twice as much total time as a Single mat.

questions.rationale: For a Single mat, prep is longer than weaving (3 vs 2). For a Double, weaving is longer (4 vs 3). For a Family, weaving is even longer (6 vs 4). Thus, as size increases, weaving time accounts for a greater proportion of the total time.
objectives: draw conclusions based on the text

questions.questionText: What is the central claim of the editorial?

choices.A: Traditional jeepneys are better for the environment than modern minibuses.
choices.B: The government should entirely abandon the PUV Modernization Program.
choices.C: While modernization is ecologically necessary, its current financial structure is unjust to poor operators.
choices.D: The government subsidy is overly generous and strains the national budget.

questions.rationale: The author explicitly states that replacing old jeepneys is an 'undeniable ecological necessity' but argues that the 'transition demands a critical look at economic equity' because it punishes the poor.
objectives: identify the main idea or central claim

questions.questionText: What is the author's attitude toward traditional jeepney drivers?

choices.A: Sympathetic and protective
choices.B: Indifferent and cold
choices.C: Critical and accusatory
choices.D: Condescending and mocking

questions.rationale: The author defends the drivers, stating the program is 'punishing the poor' and refers to them as the 'most vulnerable sectors', showing deep sympathy and protectiveness.
objectives: determine tone, purpose, and author’s attitude

questions.questionText: Which paragraph contains the author's concession to the opposing argument?

choices.A: Paragraph 1
choices.B: Paragraph 2
choices.C: Paragraph 3 (Cartoon Description)
choices.D: Paragraph 4

questions.rationale: In Paragraph 1, the author concedes the state's argument by acknowledging that replacing smoke-belching jeepneys 'is an undeniable ecological necessity.'
objectives: analyze logic and argument structure, including claims, reasons, and assumptions

questions.questionText: Which piece of evidence does the author use to support the claim that the financial burden on operators is 'staggering'?

choices.A: The fact that modern vehicles are Euro-4 compliant.
choices.B: The disparity between the 2,500,000-peso vehicle cost and the 160,000-peso subsidy.
choices.C: The depiction of the small driver in the editorial cartoon.
choices.D: The ecological damage caused by traditional jeepneys.

questions.rationale: The author contrasts the high cost of the vehicle (2.5 million) with the relatively low government subsidy (160,000) to mathematically demonstrate the immense remaining financial burden.
objectives: recognize supporting details and textual evidence

questions.questionText: An operator wants to purchase a modern jeepney costing exactly 2,500,000 pesos. The government provides the 160,000-peso subsidy which is deducted from the principal. If the bank requires the operator to pay a 10% downpayment on the remaining balance out of pocket, how much is the required downpayment?

choices.A: 234,000 pesos
choices.B: 250,000 pesos
choices.C: 160,000 pesos

questions.rationale: Cost = 2,500,000. Less subsidy (160,000) = 2,340,000 remaining balance. 10% of 2,340,000 = 234,000 pesos.
objectives: interpret a short embedded informational element such as a table, graph, or similar text-based data

questions.questionText: What does the 'tiny coin' given by the 'giant government official' in the editorial cartoon symbolize?

choices.A: The corruption of the drivers who pocket passenger fares.
choices.B: The inadequacy of the government subsidy relative to the massive cost of modernization.
choices.C: The low cost of modern jeepneys.
choices.D: The ecological benefits of the Euro-4 engine.

questions.rationale: The tiny coin labeled 'Subsidy' compared to the 'massive, incredibly heavy' minibus the driver carries symbolizes how small and insufficient the government financial help is compared to the huge burden of the transition.
objectives: interpret a short embedded informational element such as a table, graph, or similar text-based data

questions.questionText: In the first paragraph, what does 'ubiquitous' mean?

choices.A: Dangerous and illegal
choices.B: Found everywhere
choices.C: Expensive to maintain
choices.D: Rare and hard to find

questions.rationale: Traditional jeepneys are a very common sight in the Philippines; 'ubiquitous' means present, appearing, or found everywhere.
objectives: use context clues to determine meaning

questions.questionText: What does the author imply will happen if the modernization program proceeds without a 'commercially viable transition plan'?

choices.A: The public transport system will experience a severe crisis or collapse.
choices.B: The environment will immediately recover from pollution.
choices.C: Government officials will be forced to drive the modern minibuses themselves.
choices.D: Jeepney drivers will become extremely wealthy.

questions.rationale: The author warns that we must rethink the financial structuring 'before the backbone of our public transport snaps', implying a collapse of the transport system if operators are forced out by debt.
objectives: make valid inferences

questions.questionText: The argument that the modernization program is 'punishing the poor for a systemic failure' relies on which underlying assumption?

choices.A: Poor drivers intentionally choose to drive polluting vehicles to save money.
choices.B: The government has historically provided excellent public transport infrastructure.
choices.C: The environmental degradation caused by old jeepneys is the fault of the passengers.
choices.D: The lack of green, modern transport is a structural issue that individual, impoverished drivers should not have to pay to fix out of pocket.

questions.rationale: The phrase 'systemic failure' implies a broader societal or governmental shortcoming. Assuming it is unjust to make the 'poor' pay for it means the author believes structural/national problems shouldn't be fixed by financially breaking the lowest earners.
objectives: analyze logic and argument structure, including claims, reasons, and assumptions

questions.questionText: Which sentence from the final paragraph functions as its main conclusion?

choices.A: If we mandate modernization without providing a commercially viable transition plan, we are essentially punishing the poor for a systemic failure.
choices.B: Progress cannot be genuinely called progress if it leaves the most vulnerable sectors in the dust.
choices.C: We must rethink the financial structuring of this program before the backbone of our public transport snaps.
choices.D: There is no concluding sentence in the final paragraph.

questions.rationale: Sentence C is the actionable thesis and ultimate conclusion of the essay, calling for a policy rethink ('We must rethink...') based on the premises established in the earlier sentences.
objectives: locate the main idea or topic sentence
